props.name: equilibrium methanol rises with falling temperature and rising pressure

evidence.quote: heat, it is obvious that the amount of methanol in an equilibrium mixture increases as the temperature of the reaction decreases.
it is also obvious that the methanol in an equilibrium mixture increases as the pressure of the reacting gases increases.

evidence.note: preceded by 'By means of calculations based on the Nernst heat' and the line number '30'
evidence.quote: theorem, it may be shown that the amounts of methanol in equilibrium with carbon mon- oxide and hydrogen at pressures near atmos- pheric are exceedingly small.

props.statement: Because the reaction liberates heat, equilibrium methanol increases as the temperature decreases; because it involves a decrease in volume, it increases with pressure: near atmospheric pressure it is exceedingly small (less than 0.1% above 250° C.) but it increases rapidly with pressure (45% possible at 300° C. and 200 atmospheres).

props.note: the patent's account of prior art, partly citing U.S. Patents 1,201,850 and 1,271,013 and German Patent 295,202
props.statement: Prior catalysts (oxides of chromium, titanium, molybdenum, zinc, manganese; with copper turnings, wool, gauze or reduced copper oxide; co-precipitated chromium and copper oxides reduced in hydrogen) did not give satisfactory results: the precipitated mixture crumbles to powder, supports such as asbestos dilute the catalyst, and copper catalysts were not reactive at the low temperatures favorable to methanol.
